points.description: States that a linear classifier cannot handle/classify data that is not linearly separable in feature space (its limitation).
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely says linear classifiers are limited or simple, without linking to non-separable data.

points.description: States that a nonlinear classifier can handle such cases because it can form more complex (curved/nonlinear) decision boundaries.
points.partial_credit: Half if says nonlinear is better/more flexible but does not mention complex decision boundaries or non-separable data.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for saying linear classifiers fail when classes are not linearly separable and nonlinear ones succeed by forming more complex decision boundaries. Give 1 mark if only one of the two ideas is clear, or both are stated vaguely. Give 0 for wrong or unrelated answers, such as claiming nonlinear is just faster or simpler.
